task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update on Rivermoth Library's overdue-fine decision and what borrowers still owe or need to return.

facts.text: Rivermoth Library's board voted unanimously on Monday, Aug. 31, 2026, to end daily overdue fines on borrowed books beginning Oct. 1.
The library will also erase existing book-overdue fines, which total $15,200 on its account ledger.
Charges for lost or damaged materials, printing and equipment rental will not be erased by this policy.
Approximately 620 accounts are blocked solely by book-overdue fines in the current ledger and would regain borrowing access when those fines are erased, provided no other block applies.
Other blocked accounts may still owe replacement charges or have long-overdue items, according to circulation manager Leda Sorn.
Borrowers must still return books, and reminders will continue to be sent before an item is classified as lost.
Under the library's unchanged lost-item policy, a book still unreturned 35 calendar days after its due date becomes subject to a replacement charge.
Returning an undamaged book removes that book's replacement charge; unrelated charges on the account remain.
Last year's overdue-fine receipts were $9,400; a staff-time review valued the labor used to administer those fines at an estimated $18,000.
The staff-time estimate is not cash the library will receive after the change; staff will be reassigned to other circulation work.
The library budget assumes losing the fine receipts and does not count the erased ledger balances as a new cash expense.
Sorn said, "We want the book back on the shelf, not a small debt that keeps its borrower outside."
Parent Neri Wren said a past overdue balance had made her reluctant to ask staff about another missing book.
Wren said, "I can come in with the book instead of coming in ready to explain the bill."
The library has not measured how many restored accounts will resume borrowing after Oct. 1.
Board member Torin Vail asked for quarterly reporting of return times and missing-item rates.
The board approved that reporting request but did not set a target increase in circulation.
The policy covers all four branches and the mobile library, but not materials borrowed through a separate university system.
Rivermoth Library has waived children's book fines during occasional summer-return campaigns since 2013.
The new vote is a continuing policy rather than another time-limited summer campaign.
